headline: Mandatory Parking Tags and Seasonal Road Status
reservation: While the park has no entrance fee, valid parking tags are required for any vehicle stopping for more than 15 minutes. Campground reservations must be made via official federal portals well in advance, especially for October foliage. Access to Kuwohi and Cades Cove may have vehicle-free windows; check the official NPS schedule.

days.title: High Ridges and Boundaries

stops.name: Newfound Gap
stops.detail: Stand on the Tennessee-North Carolina state line where the Appalachian Trail crosses this major mountain pass.

stops.name: Kuwohi (formerly Clingmans Dome)
stops.detail: Walk the steep paved path to the observation tower for the highest point in the park, subject to seasonal road openings.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for the climb and return due to winding roads and potential fog.
days.note: Temperatures at Kuwohi are often 10–20 degrees cooler than Gatlinburg; bring layers.

days.title: Heritage and Wildlife of the Cove

stops.name: Cades Cove Loop Road
stops.detail: Drive the 11-mile one-way loop to see 19th-century cabins, churches, and frequent sightings of white-tailed deer or black bears.

stops.name: Abrams Falls Trail
stops.detail: Embark on a moderate hike from the loop to a high-volume waterfall; allow ample time for the return walk.

days.driving: The 11-mile loop can take 2–4 hours depending on wildlife traffic; plan accordingly.
days.note: Check the official NPS schedule for 'Vehicle-Free Wednesdays' if you plan to walk or cycle the loop.

days.title: River Valleys and Farm Life

stops.name: Oconaluftee Visitor Center
stops.detail: Explore the Mountain Farm Museum’s historic buildings and look for the elk herd often grazing in nearby fields.

stops.name: Deep Creek Waterfalls
stops.detail: Follow the trail to see Tom Branch Falls and Juney Whank Falls in a lush, creek-side setting near Bryson City.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes to transfer between Oconaluftee and the Deep Creek area.
days.note: Elk are wild animals; stay at least 50 yards away and never approach them for photos.

intel.title: Parking Tag Compliance
intel.text: Purchase your daily or weekly parking tag at visitor centers or automated kiosks before heading to trailheads. A tag does not guarantee a spot at popular locations like Alum Cave or Laurel Falls.

intel.title: Mountain Topography Limits
intel.text: Expect total loss of signal in deep valleys and throughout the Cades Cove area. Use the Sugarlands or Oconaluftee Wi-Fi to download necessary maps before heading uphill.

intel.title: Gateway Service Hubs
intel.text: No gasoline is sold within the park boundaries. Fill your tank in Gatlinburg, Townsend, or Cherokee before starting the Newfound Gap Road ascent.

intel.title: Peak Foliage Traffic
intel.text: During October, travel times can double due to leaf-peeping traffic. Mid-week visits and sunrise starts are the only ways to mitigate the heaviest congestion.

intel.title: Winter Road Closures
intel.text: Newfound Gap Road (US-441) frequently closes for snow or ice; Kuwohi Road is seasonally closed from December through March. Check the official NPS Twitter or site for real-time gate status.

plan.arrival: Fly into McGhee Tyson Airport (TYS), pick up a rental car, and stock up on picnic supplies in Maryville or Sevierville before checking into your Tennessee-side base.
plan.vehicle: Automatic transmissions are recommended for steep mountain grades; check rental agreements for restrictions on unpaved secondary roads.
plan.goldenHour: Newfound Gap provides an expansive eastern view for sunrise, while Morton Overlook is a famed spot for sunset, provided clouds don't obscure the ridge.
